This causes calcium to leak continuously, potentially damaging muscle tissue.

Science.title: Water as we've never known it: Physicists test water beyond Earth-like conditions
Science.summary: Water isn't always as it seems. Under extreme conditions, such as those found on other planets, it has been discovered to change its atomic structure, giving it the means to alter its appearance and other properties.

Science.title: Scientists find a way to fight Alzheimer’s brain damage without removing toxic tau
Science.summary: Scientists have found a promising way to protect the brain from Alzheimer’s-related damage by blocking immune cells that contribute to the destruction of neurons. In mice, the treatment preserved roughly 40% more tissue in memory centers and improved memory, even without removing harmful tau protein buildup.

Science.title: Vast new fossil record challenges story of Earth’s ‘big five’ mass extinctions
Science.summary: Nature, Published online: 20 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03316-4 An artificial-intelligence model trained on nearly four million fossils suggests that three of the extinction events might have happened more gradually than previously thought.

Science.title: NASA reveals 16 stunning galaxies hiding cosmic chaos
Science.summary: NASA's stunning new gallery of 16 galaxies reveals colossal black hole jets, explosive star formation, and spectacular cosmic collisions through the combined power of Chandra, James Webb, Hubble, and other telescopes. These extraordinary images expose the hidden forces shaping galaxies across the universe and offer clues about the Milky Way's own past and future.

Science.title: Diverse and sustained social activities may boost cognition in older age
Science.summary: Diverse and sustained social activities may boost cognitive performance and slow the decline in brain health associated with aging, suggest the findings of a large international study, published online in the Journal of Epidemiology & Community Health.

Science.title: NASA solves a strange mystery hidden inside asteroid Bennu’s boulders
Science.summary: NASA scientists have finally uncovered why asteroid Bennu loses heat so quickly despite being covered in massive boulders. Samples returned to Earth reveal that its rocks are filled with hidden cracks, solving a mystery that has puzzled researchers for years.

Science.title: From seafloor depths to fishing activity, free software brings ocean data together
Science.summary: For scientists studying the ocean, finding the right data can sometimes be as challenging as figuring out what to do with it. Want to know seafloor depth, the location of underwater mountains or sea surface temperatures? The information exists, but it can take considerable time and computer coding to pull it together from different sources and get it into the proper format.

Science.title: Can’t make it to the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art for the 'Star Wars' display? This is the companion book set you’re looking for!
Science.summary: Prepare for a lightspeed tour of Lucas's lifetime collection ofpaintings, posters, comics, concept art, and illustrations

Science.title: Soybean waste yields 3D-printable material that could help repair skin
Science.summary: Transforming a soybean processing byproduct into a material for skin protection and repair is the prospect outlined by a study that used okara, a residue from the production of tofu and soy-based beverages, to obtain a bioactive, biodegradable, 3D-printable biomaterial.

Science.title: The moon is shrinking. 10,000 cracks on the lunar surface reveal by how much
Science.summary: One new study shows how much the moon has diminished over time.

Science.title: Body clock disruptions contribute to one in four cases of depression, suggests large study
Science.summary: Nature, Published online: 20 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03359-7 Evidence grows for ‘circadian depression’, but more evidence is needed to change diagnosis and treatment guidelines.

Science.title: Your aging brain may be trading memory for something more valuable
Science.summary: The aging brain may be undergoing a remarkable transformation rather than simply losing its abilities, shifting its focus from remembering details to understanding the bigger picture. Scientists suggest this change could be an evolutionary adaptation that helps older adults develop wisdom and share decades of knowledge with younger generations.

Science.title: Tofu is the winner. Scientist creates new holistic scoring system to measure the impact of food
Science.summary: Consumers are increasingly confronted with conflicting information surrounding how much protein they should have and which protein sources are healthiest, most sustainable, and best value for money. Cambridge research has uncovered the truth.

Science.title: Where El Niño may impact California coastal areas this winter
Science.summary: Driving across Highway 37 in the San Francisco Bay Area on the best of days already feels like driving on top of water. Buffeted on both sides by marshlands hosting egrets, herons, ducks and a handful of endangered species, the sea-level highway is a major connector linking Marin, Sonoma, Napa and Solano counties.

Science.title: Why is it so hard to spot a liar? Expert explains the psychology of deception
Science.summary: From The Traitors to everyday life, we often mistake nervousness, confidence or group suspicion for signs of deception. Dr Nadja Heym, Associate Professor in Personality Psychology and Psychopathology, explains why spotting a liar is harder than we think.

Science.title: A gene variant triples the risk of getting Alzheimer's disease — fat buildup in brain cells may be to blame, study finds
Science.summary: A gene variant called APOE4 is the biggest genetic risk factor for Alzheimer's disease. Scientists are finally figuring out how it works.

Science.title: Scientists reach the ultimate quantum limit on a surface
Science.summary: Scientists have achieved a quantum breakthrough by creating an ultra-clean surface where individual molecules can maintain their delicate quantum properties at the fundamental limit. The discovery could unlock unprecedented control over molecules and help drive the next generation of quantum technologies.

Science.title: Could 'body clocks' play a role in depression? Study proposes a new 'circadian' subtype
Science.summary: Researchers propose a new subtype of depression linked to body-clock patterns.

Science.title: Caribbean islands were once the center of diversity for barn owls
Science.summary: Legend has it that a giant elfin, owl-like creature called the chickcharney haunts the islands of the Bahamas. Those who encounter this cryptid on cordial terms are said to be blessed with good luck. Those who disrespect the chickcharney, however, don't fare as well. "If you see one shoe in the field, it means that chickcharney came, picked up this person and took them away," said Jessica Oswald, recounting a story she was told in the Bahamas.

Science.title: Northern Australia is a 'lifeboat' for critically endangered green sawfish
Science.summary: Green sawfish, distinguished by their long, sharklike bodies and tooth-lined "saw" on the front of their heads, are on the verge of extinction, largely due to overfishing and habitat loss.

Science.title: Butterfly wing patterns make motion hard to read
Science.summary: Nature, Published online: 20 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03062-7 Movement can expose camouflaged prey, yet whether colour patterns help moving prey to avoid capture is a long-standing puzzle. Butterfly wings might offer an answer.

Science.title: Nature ’s job-satisfaction survey highlights the changing geography of science
Science.summary: Nature, Published online: 20 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03327-1 A higher proportion of scientists in China and India report feeling optimistic about the future than in the United States and several European countries.

Science.summary: 'More human than human. That's not a slogan; it's a shackle'

Science.title: Undeciphered Voynich manuscript may have been bound out of order, study finds
Science.summary: Experts argue that the mysterious Voynich manuscript was incorrectly bound — a discovery that "moves the ball" in finally deciphering the 15th-century document.

Science.title: Distrust in the media and courts can cause democratic backsliding, study suggests
Science.summary: Democratic backsliding can be tricky to spot.

Science.summary: Brick by brick ... the truth is out there. You can now own a little piece of that with this 1,478-piece Lego set

Science.title: Male seahorse pouch proteins may help remove toxic waste from developing embryos
Science.summary: Male seahorses, fishes that belong to the Syngnathidae family, show a distinctive reproductive strategy in which males carry developing embryos in a brood pouch. Their most distinctive feature is the brood pouch on the ventral side of the male fish, into which the female fish transfers her eggs.

Science.title: Machine learning reveals potential warning signal for polar vortex disruptions
Science.summary: The polar vortex, a swirling mass of cold air encircling the North Pole, is sometimes disrupted by sudden stratospheric warming (SSW) events, unleashing waves of frigid air that penetrate farther south than usual. Temperatures across North America and Europe drop precipitously when this happens, but such events remain hard to predict, meaning we can't easily warn people when SSW is imminent.

Science.title: Is it ‘moon-stroke’, or a chill?
Science.summary: Nature, Published online: 20 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02975-7 An explanation for the injurious effect of sleeping in the moonlight, and a proponent of all-electronic televisions, in this week’s pick from the Nature archive.

Science.title: Will this sleep-disorder drug be the next big blockbuster?
Science.summary: Nature, Published online: 20 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03310-w Orexin agonists have been approved for the treatment of a type of narcolepsy, yet they could also treat conditions across the health spectrum.

Science.title: Judging faces without personality labels uncovers key patterns in first impressions
Science.summary: Imagine sitting on a city bus full of strangers. Look around at the people riding with you. If you needed help, how would you choose whom to trust? By scanning people's faces, your brain is already making interpretations about their personalities by judging certain facial features.

Science.title: Red light, white light: How to preserve your night vision while using stargazing apps
Science.summary: The right apps can take a lot of the work out of stargazing, but they can also stop your eyes from adjusting to the dark. Here's how to use them without ruining your skywatching.

Science.title: Could a $200K bond for satellites paid before launch prevent a space junk disaster in orbit? Here's why some scientists think so
Science.summary: The space around Earth is turning into a junkyard. Researchers think a refundable deposit scheme could force satellite operators to clean up their act before a tipping point is reached.
